title: ERA5-Land Reanalysis (hourly and monthly, 0.1°)
description: ERA5-Land is a global land-surface reanalysis produced by replaying the land component (H-TESSEL) of the ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis forced by ERA5 atmospheric fields, from January 1950 to present. It provides hourly land variables (temperature, precipitation, soil water in four layers, evaporation, runoff, snow, energy fluxes) on a regular 0.1° grid, with a separate post-processed monthly-averaged product.
purpose: Offers a gap-free, physically consistent record of near-surface climate and land water-balance variables over all of Algeria since 1950, useful as a reference for temperature, evaporation and soil-moisture context where observations are sparse.

spatial_extent.description: Global land surface on a regular 0.1° x 0.1° latitude–longitude grid (native: octahedral reduced Gaussian grid TCo1279, about 9 km). The CDS form allows area sub-setting, so an Algeria box can be requested directly, but the user must define it.

temporal_extent.description: January 1950 to present. Hourly data (DOI 10.24381/cds.e2161bac) and monthly averages (DOI 10.24381/cds.68d2bb30). Near-real-time ERA5-Land-T is available about 5 days behind real time (monthly means about 5 days after month end) and is replaced by consolidated ERA5-Land about two months later.

crs: EPSG:4326 (WGS 84, regular latitude–longitude grid as distributed by the CDS)

variables.name: 2m temperature (t2m)
variables.description: Air temperature at 2 m above the surface

variables.name: Total precipitation (tp)
variables.description: Accumulated liquid and frozen precipitation (taken from the ERA5 forcing)

variables.name: Volumetric soil water layers 1–4 (swvl1–swvl4)
variables.description: Soil water in layers 0–7, 7–28, 28–100 and 100–289 cm

variables.name: Total evaporation
variables.description: Accumulated evaporation including a simplified representation of transpiration; negative values denote evaporation

variables.name: Potential evaporation
variables.description: Computed in ERA5-Land as open-water (pan) evaporation

variables.name: Skin temperature (skt)
variables.description: Temperature of the uppermost surface layer

processing: ERA5-Land runs the H-TESSEL land surface model (IFS cycle CY45R1) offline, forced by ERA5 near-surface meteorology, with air temperature, humidity and pressure lapse-rate corrected to the higher-resolution ERA5-Land orography. No observations are assimilated directly; observations influence the product only through the ERA5 forcing. Data are produced on the TCo1279 grid and regridded to 0.1° for the CDS.
validation: The ESSD data paper (Muñoz-Sabater et al. 2021) reports added value relative to ERA5 for soil moisture, lake description and river discharge, comparable energy-cycle results, and mixed snow-depth performance depending on location and altitude. No single global accuracy figure is stated on the CDS page.
limitations: Precipitation is inherited from the ERA5 atmospheric forcing; the land replay does not add new precipitation information.

The CDS variable description warns that potential evaporation 'can give unrealistic results in arid conditions due to too strong evaporation forced by dry air'; in ERA5-Land it is computed as open-water (pan) evaporation.

Monthly-averaged accumulated variables for September 2022–February 2024 are known to be incorrect and will not be replaced; ECMWF advises using the monthly averaged reanalysis by hour of day at 00:00 instead.
No uncertainty fields are provided; ECMWF suggests using ERA5 ensemble spread as a proxy. Uncertainty is larger in early decades with fewer observations.
Lake depth and area are held constant and lake water balance is not modelled, which affects reservoir-dominated grid cells.

algeria_notes: ERA5-Land gives complete coverage of both the semi-arid north and the hyper-arid Sahara, but its rainfall is ERA5 model precipitation and should be checked against gauges or CHIRPS in the Tell. At 0.1° (about 11 km) the lapse-rate correction helps over the Tell Atlas and Aurès, but valley–ridge contrasts are still smoothed. Potential evaporation is flagged by ECMWF as unreliable in arid conditions, which matters for most of Algeria; reservoirs are not represented as dynamic water bodies.
